title: Big-O Notation in 60 Seconds (Java) | DSA #1 #shorts
description:
DSA in 60 Seconds #1: Big-O notation, explained with Java.

Two Java methods answer the same question, does this array contain a duplicate? The nested-loop version compares every pair: O(n²), about a trillion comparisons for a million items. The HashSet version checks each item once: O(n), about a million steps. Big-O describes how running time grows as the input grows; drop constants, keep the biggest term. Common complexities: O(1), O(log n), O(n), O(n log n), O(n²).

LeetCode 217: Contains Duplicate.
Comparison counts are approximate.

lines: Two Java methods. Same answer. With a million items, one finishes instantly. The other takes minutes.
Big-O describes how your running time grows as the input grows. Not seconds, but the shape of the growth.
To find a duplicate, the slow way compares every pair with two nested loops. Double the input, four times the work. That's O(n²).
The fast way walks the array once, and remembers what it has seen in a HashSet. Each lookup is O(1), so the whole thing is O(n).
From best to worst: O(1), O(log n), O(n), O(n log n), and O(n²). Drop the constants, and keep the biggest term.
In interviews, the brute force is just the start. They want O(n). This is DSA number one.
